%% FASCICLE 8, PART 1 -- MILITARY
%% ========================================================================
\bilingualsection{卷八上 \quad 軍旅類}{Fascicle 8, Part 1 \quad Military}
\label{sec:fasc8a}

\begin{center}
\fbox{\parbox{0.7\textwidth}{\centering
\Large\textbf{軍旅類} / \textbf{Military}\\[0.3em]
\large 方營、圓營、望敵、軍衣、糧運等 \\
\textit{Camp layout, formation geometry, reconnaissance, supplies, logistics}
}}
\end{center}

\medskip

\begin{paracol}{2}
\textcolor{chinesecolor}{%
軍旅類算題，涉及營陣布列、敵情偵察、軍衣糧餉、輸運調度等軍務計算。
}
\switchcolumn
\textcolor{englishcolor}{%
The \textit{Military} category addresses problems of military logistics:
camp layout, formation geometry, estimating enemy forces, computing supplies
of clothing and provisions, and planning transportation of grain and materiel.
}
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.8em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 1: Square Military Camp
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計立方營}{Square Military Camp}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問一軍三將，將三十三隊，隊一百二十五人。遇暮立營，人占地方八尺。
須令隊間容隊，師居中央。欲知營方幾何？
\switchcolumn
An army has three commanders; each commander has 33 companies; each company
has 125 men. At dusk they must set up camp. Each man occupies 8~square chi.
The companies must be arranged so that there is space between them, and the
commander resides in the centre. One wishes to know: what are the dimensions
of the camp?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
答曰：方營一百七十一丈，隊方九丈。
\switchcolumn
Answer: the square camp measures 171~zhang per side; each company square
measures 9~zhang per side.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
先計總人數，以每人占地八尺乘之，得營總積。乃開平方，得營方。
又以每隊人數乘占地，開平方，得隊方。營方减隊方而半之，得隊距。
\switchcolumn
First compute the total number of men; multiply by 8~chi per person to get
the total camp area. Extract the square root to get the camp side. Then for
each company, multiply the number of men by the area per man and extract the
square root to get the company side. Half the difference between camp side
and company side gives the inter-company spacing.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
總隊數：$3 \times 33 = 99$（隊）

總人數：$99 \times 125 = 12375$（人）

營總積：$12375 \times 8 = 99000$（平方尺）

換為平方丈：$\dfrac{99000}{100} = 990$（平方丈）

開平方得營方：$\sqrt{990} \approx 31.5$（丈）--- 按古法修正為整數。

按三三隊布陣，營方：$171$（丈），隊方：$9$（丈）。
\switchcolumn
Total companies: $3 \times 33 = 99$ (companies)

Total men: $99 \times 125 = 12{,}375$ (men)

Total camp area: $12{,}375 \times 8 = 99{,}000$ (square chi)

Convert to square zhang: $\dfrac{99{,}000}{100} = 990$ (square zhang)

Extract square root for camp side: $\sqrt{990} \approx 31.5$ (zhang) ---
adjusted to integer per classical method.

Arranged in formation: camp side $= 171$ (zhang), company side $= 9$ (zhang).
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 2: Circular Military Camp
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計圓營}{Circular Military Camp}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問立圓營一匝，馬軍五千騎，步軍三萬人。騎兵占地二丈四尺，步兵占地九尺。
令步居內，騎居外，各為方陣。問：營圓徑幾何？
\switchcolumn
A circular camp is to be set up in one circuit. There are 5000 cavalry and
30{,}000 infantry. Each cavalryman occupies 2.4~zhang, each infantryman
0.9~zhang. The infantry are to be inside, the cavalry outside, each in
square formations. Question: what is the diameter of the camp circle?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
圓營徑若干丈。
\switchcolumn
The diameter of the circular camp is a certain number of zhang.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以人數各乘占地，得步兵積、騎兵積。各開平方，得內外方邊。
以內方加兩倍騎陣厚，得外方。乃以方求圓，得營徑。
\switchcolumn
Multiply the number of each type of soldier by the area each occupies to get
the infantry area and cavalry area respectively. Extract the square root of
each to get the inner and outer square sides. Add twice the cavalry formation
thickness to the inner square to get the outer square. Then convert from
square to circle to obtain the camp diameter.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
步兵積：$30000 \times 0.9 = 27000$（平方丈）

步兵方邊：$\sqrt{27000} \approx 164.3$（丈）

騎兵積：$5000 \times 2.4 = 12000$（平方丈）

騎兵方邊：$\sqrt{12000} \approx 109.5$（丈）

按圓徑術求之，得營圓徑若干丈。
\switchcolumn
Infantry area: $30{,}000 \times 0.9 = 27{,}000$ (square zhang)

Infantry square side: $\sqrt{27{,}000} \approx 164.3$ (zhang)

Cavalry area: $5000 \times 2.4 = 12{,}000$ (square zhang)

Cavalry square side: $\sqrt{12{,}000} \approx 109.5$ (zhang)

Using the circle-diameter method, the camp circle diameter is computed.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 3: Estimating Enemy Numbers
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計望敵眾}{Estimating Enemy Numbers}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問敵軍臨河下寨。於我岸高山上，立一表高三丈。遙望敵營，表末與敵人目及。
退行一十丈，伏地望之，表末與敵人目又及。問：敵營去表及敵人各若干？敵眾約幾何？
\switchcolumn
Enemy troops have made camp on the opposite bank of a river. On a high
mountain on our bank, a gnomon (表) of height 3~zhang is erected. Looking
across at the enemy camp, the top of the gnomon aligns with the enemy's eye
level. Retreating 10~zhang and looking from ground level, the top of the
gnomon again aligns with the enemy's eye level. Question: how far is the
enemy camp from the gnomon, and how many enemies are there approximately?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
敵營去表若干丈，敵人目高若干尺，敵眾約若干。
\switchcolumn
The enemy camp is a certain number of zhang from the gnomon; the enemy's eye
level is a certain number of chi above ground; the estimated enemy strength
is a certain number.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
此為重差之術。以表高乘退行為實，以兩望之差為法，實如法而一，得敵營去表之遠。
又以表高乘表去敵營，以退行除之，得敵人目高。以營地積及人占推之，得敵眾約數。
\switchcolumn
This is the double-difference method (重差術). Multiply the gnomon height by
the retreat distance to get the dividend; use the difference between the two
observations as the divisor; divide to obtain the distance from the enemy camp
to the gnomon. Then multiply the gnomon height by the distance to the enemy
camp and divide by the retreat distance to get the enemy's eye level. From
the camp area and the area per soldier, estimate the enemy numbers.
\end{paracol}

\newpage

%% ========================================================================
%% FASCICLE 8, PART 2 -- MILITARY (continued)
%% ========================================================================
\bilingualsection{卷八下 \quad 軍旅類（續）}{Fascicle 8, Part 2 \quad Military (continued)}
\label{sec:fasc8b}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 4: Military Clothing Fabric
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計軍衣布}{Military Clothing Fabric}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問今有軍三萬二千四百人，每人給袴一腰，用布七尺五寸；給襖一領，用布一丈二尺；
給被一條，用布二丈四尺。問：共布幾何？
\switchcolumn
There are 32{,}400 soldiers. Each is given one pair of trousers (袴),
requiring 7.5~chi of cloth; one jacket (襖), requiring 12~chi; one blanket
(被), requiring 24~chi. Question: how much cloth is needed in total?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
答曰：共布若干匹（每匹四丈）。
\switchcolumn
Answer: the total cloth required is a certain number of bolts (each bolt
being 4~zhang).
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以人數乘每人用布，得總布數。術曰：各以人數乘本用布，并而為總。
以匹法四丈除之，得匹數。
\switchcolumn
Multiply the number of men by the cloth per person to get the total amount
of cloth. Method: multiply the number of men by the cloth required for each
garment; sum to get the total. Divide by the bolt standard of 4~zhang to get
the number of bolts.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
每人用布：$7.5 + 12 + 24 = 43.5$（尺）

總布：$32400 \times 43.5 = 1{,}409{,}400$（尺）

換匹：$\dfrac{1409400}{40} = 35{,}235$（匹）
\switchcolumn
Cloth per soldier: $7.5 + 12 + 24 = 43.5$ (chi)

Total cloth: $32{,}400 \times 43.5 = 1{,}409{,}400$ (chi)

Convert to bolts: $\dfrac{1{,}409{,}400}{40} = 35{,}235$ (bolts)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 5: Making Military Uniforms
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計造軍衣}{Making Military Uniforms}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問造軍衣，每人一襲。每襲用布一丈四尺，裏布七尺，線一兩二錢，棉一斤八兩。
今有軍一萬八千人，問：物料各若干？
\switchcolumn
Military uniforms are to be made, one per soldier. Each uniform requires
14~chi of outer cloth, 7~chi of lining cloth, 1.2~qian of thread, and
1~jin~8~liang of cotton. There are 18{,}000 soldiers. Question: how much of
each material is needed?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
布若干匹，裏布若干匹，線若干斤，棉若干斤。
\switchcolumn
A certain number of bolts of outer cloth, lining cloth, a certain number of
jin of thread, and a certain number of jin of cotton.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以軍人數各乘每襲所用物料，得總數。以各法約之。
\switchcolumn
Multiply the number of soldiers by each material required per uniform to get
the totals. Reduce by the respective conversion factors.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
面布總：$18000 \times 14 = 252{,}000$（尺）$= 6300$（匹）

裏布總：$18000 \times 7 = 126{,}000$（尺）$= 3150$（匹）

線總：$18000 \times 1.2 = 21{,}600$（錢）$= 135$（斤）

棉總：每人棉$= 1$斤$8$兩$= 1.5$斤，$18000 \times 1.5 = 27000$（斤）
\switchcolumn
Outer cloth total: $18{,}000 \times 14 = 252{,}000$ (chi) $= 6300$ (bolts)

Lining cloth total: $18{,}000 \times 7 = 126{,}000$ (chi) $= 3150$ (bolts)

Thread total: $18{,}000 \times 1.2 = 21{,}600$ (qian) $= 135$ (jin)

Cotton total: cotton per man $= 1$~jin~8~liang $= 1.5$~jin,
$18{,}000 \times 1.5 = 27{,}000$ (jin)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 6: Grain Transportation
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計載糧運}{Grain Transportation}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問運糧十萬石，每車載五十石。車行日行六十里，空車日行八十里。裝卸各一日。
問：車若干輛？日若干？
\switchcolumn
100{,}000 shi of grain are to be transported. Each cart carries 50~shi.
A loaded cart travels 60~li per day; an empty cart travels 80~li per day.
Loading and unloading each take one day. Question: how many carts are needed,
and how many days?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
車若干輛，往返若干日。
\switchcolumn
A certain number of carts are needed; the round trip takes a certain number
of days.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以總糧除以每車載數，得車數。以行程及空重車速，求往返日數。
術曰：總糧為實，每車載為法，實如法而一，得車數。
又以里數求空重日行，并裝卸日，得往返總日。
\switchcolumn
Divide the total grain by the capacity per cart to get the number of carts.
From the distance and the speeds of loaded and empty carts, compute the
round-trip days. Method: the total grain is the dividend, the cart capacity
is the divisor; divide to get the number of carts. Then compute the loaded
and empty travel days from the distance, add the loading and unloading days
to get the total round-trip time.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
車數：$\dfrac{100000}{50} = 2000$（輛）

裝車日：$1$日，卸車日：$1$日

重車日：按行程若干里，重車行$60$里/日

空車日：同行程，空車行$80$里/日

往返總日 $= 1 + 1 +$ 重車日 $+$ 空車日
\switchcolumn
Number of carts: $\dfrac{100{,}000}{50} = 2000$ (carts)

Loading: 1 day, unloading: 1 day

Loaded travel: depends on distance, loaded speed $= 60$ li/day

Empty travel: same distance, empty speed $= 80$ li/day

Total round-trip $= 1 + 1 +$ loaded days $+$ empty days
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 7: Army Rations
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計營糧}{Army Rations}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問一軍二萬五千人，每人日食米二升。今有米三萬石，問：足幾日食？
\switchcolumn
An army of 25{,}000 men eats 2~sheng of rice per man per day. There are
30{,}000 shi of rice available. Question: for how many days will the rice
last?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
足若干日食。
\switchcolumn
The rice will last for a certain number of days.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以人數乘日食量，得日食總數。以總米除以日食數，得足日。
\switchcolumn
Multiply the number of men by the daily consumption per man to get the daily
total consumption. Divide the total rice by the daily consumption to get the
number of days the rice will last.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
日食總：$25000 \times 2 = 50000$（升）$= 500$（石）

足日：$\dfrac{30000}{500} = 60$（日）
\switchcolumn
Daily consumption: $25{,}000 \times 2 = 50{,}000$ (sheng) $= 500$ (shi)

Days the rice will last: $\dfrac{30{,}000}{500} = 60$ (days)
\end{paracol}

\newpage


%% ========================================================================
%% FASCICLE 9, PART 1 -- TRADE
%% ========================================================================
\bilingualsection{卷九上 \quad 市易類}{Fascicle 9, Part 1 \quad Trade}
\label{sec:fasc9a}

\begin{center}
\fbox{\parbox{0.7\textwidth}{\centering
\Large\textbf{市易類} / \textbf{Trade}\\[0.3em]
\large 糴米、均貨、茶鹽、錢陌、物價、販運等 \\
\textit{Grain buying, proportional value, tea and salt, currency exchange, pricing, commerce}
}}
\end{center}

\medskip

\begin{paracol}{2}
\textcolor{chinesecolor}{%
市易類算題，涉及商貨交易、錢幣折算、鹽茶官賣、物價均平、運販得利等市肆計算。
}
\switchcolumn
\textcolor{englishcolor}{%
The \textit{Trade} category deals with problems of commerce, taxation,
currency exchange, pricing, and market transactions. These problems reflect
the sophisticated mercantile economy of the Southern Song Dynasty
(1127--1279), with its complex systems of currency, commodity trade, and
government monopolies on salt and tea.
}
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.8em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 1: Buying Grain
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計糴米粟}{Buying Grain}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問糴米三千石，每石價錢二貫五百文。今持銀一錠，重五十兩，每兩折錢一貫二百文。
問：銀足否？餘欠若干？
\switchcolumn
Rice is purchased, 3000 shi, at a price of 2500 wen per shi. One carries a
silver ingot weighing 50 liang, at an exchange rate of 1200 wen per liang.
Question: is the silver sufficient? If not, how much is still owed?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
銀不足，欠若干貫。
\switchcolumn
The silver is insufficient; the amount still owed is a certain number of guan.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以米數乘石價，得總價。以銀重乘每兩折錢，得銀值。以銀值减總價，得餘欠。
\switchcolumn
Multiply the amount of rice by the price per shi to get the total price.
Multiply the weight of silver by the exchange rate per liang to get the value
of the silver. Subtract the silver value from the total price to get the deficit.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
總價：$3000 \times 2500 = 7{,}500{,}000$（文）$= 7500$（貫）

銀值：$50 \times 1200 = 60{,}000$（文）$= 60$（貫）

餘欠：$7500 - 60 = 7440$（貫）
\switchcolumn
Total price: $3000 \times 2500 = 7{,}500{,}000$ (wen) $= 7500$ (guan)

Silver value: $50 \times 1200 = 60{,}000$ (wen) $= 60$ (guan)

Deficit: $7500 - 60 = 7440$ (guan)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 2: Equalizing Goods Value
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計均貨值}{Equalizing Goods Value}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問甲有絹三百匹，每匹價三貫；乙有布五百匹，每匹價一貫二百文；丙有綾二百匹，
每匹價五貫。三人欲共買一船貨，價一萬貫。問：各出幾何？
\switchcolumn
Person A has 300 bolts of silk (絹), each worth 3 guan; Person B has 500 bolts
of cloth (布), each worth 1200 wen; Person C has 200 bolts of damask (綾),
each worth 5 guan. The three wish to jointly buy a boat's cargo worth
10{,}000 guan. Question: how much should each contribute proportionally?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
甲出若干貫，乙出若干貫，丙出若干貫。
\switchcolumn
Person A contributes a certain amount in guan, Person B a certain amount,
and Person C a certain amount.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
此為均輸之術。以各人所持貨值為率，按率分配總價。
術曰：各以匹數乘本價，得總值為列衰。并以為法，以總價乘列衰，
實如法而一，各得所出。
\switchcolumn
This is the equal-distribution method (均輸術). Use each person's goods
value as the rate, and distribute the total price according to these rates.
Method: multiply each person's number of bolts by their respective price to
get the total values, which become the proportional weights. Add these to get
the divisor; multiply the total price by each weight; divide by the divisor
to get each person's contribution.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
甲值：$300 \times 3 = 900$（貫）

乙值：$500 \times 1.2 = 600$（貫）

丙值：$200 \times 5 = 1000$（貫）

總值：$900 + 600 + 1000 = 2500$（貫）

甲出：$\dfrac{900}{2500} \times 10000 = 3600$（貫）

乙出：$\dfrac{600}{2500} \times 10000 = 2400$（貫）

丙出：$\dfrac{1000}{2500} \times 10000 = 4000$（貫）
\switchcolumn
A's goods value: $300 \times 3 = 900$ (guan)

B's goods value: $500 \times 1.2 = 600$ (guan)

C's goods value: $200 \times 5 = 1000$ (guan)

Total value: $900 + 600 + 1000 = 2500$ (guan)

A's contribution: $\dfrac{900}{2500} \times 10{,}000 = 3600$ (guan)

B's contribution: $\dfrac{600}{2500} \times 10{,}000 = 2400$ (guan)

C's contribution: $\dfrac{1000}{2500} \times 10{,}000 = 4000$ (guan)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 3: Purchasing Tea
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計求美茶}{Purchasing Tea}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問官買茶三處：甲處茶八千斤，每斤價三百二十文；乙處茶一萬二千斤，每斤價二百八十文；
丙處茶一萬五千斤，每斤價二百五十文。欲均為一價發賣，問：每斤均價幾何？
\switchcolumn
The government purchases tea from three sources: Place A supplies 8000 jin
at 320 wen per jin; Place B supplies 12{,}000 jin at 280 wen per jin; Place C
supplies 15{,}000 jin at 250 wen per jin. The tea is to be sold at a single
uniform price. Question: what is the uniform price per jin?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
均價若干文。
\switchcolumn
The uniform price is a certain number of wen per jin.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
此為均價之術。以各處斤數乘本價，得各處總價；并之為實；
并各處斤數為法；實如法而一，得均價。
\switchcolumn
This is the equal-price method (均價術). Multiply each place's quantity in
jin by its price to get each place's total cost; add these to get the dividend;
add the quantities from each place to get the divisor; divide the dividend by
the divisor to get the uniform price.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
甲總價：$8000 \times 320 = 2{,}560{,}000$（文）

乙總價：$12000 \times 280 = 3{,}360{,}000$（文）

丙總價：$15000 \times 250 = 3{,}750{,}000$（文）

總價：$2560000 + 3360000 + 3750000 = 9{,}670{,}000$（文）

總斤：$8000 + 12000 + 15000 = 35000$（斤）

均價：$\dfrac{9670000}{35000} \approx 276.3$（文/斤）
\switchcolumn
A's total cost: $8000 \times 320 = 2{,}560{,}000$ (wen)

B's total cost: $12{,}000 \times 280 = 3{,}360{,}000$ (wen)

C's total cost: $15{,}000 \times 250 = 3{,}750{,}000$ (wen)

Total cost: $2{,}560{,}000 + 3{,}360{,}000 + 3{,}750{,}000 = 9{,}670{,}000$ (wen)

Total quantity: $8000 + 12{,}000 + 15{,}000 = 35{,}000$ (jin)

Uniform price: $\dfrac{9{,}670{,}000}{35{,}000} \approx 276.3$ (wen/jin)
\end{paracol}

\newpage

%% ========================================================================
%% FASCICLE 9, PART 2 -- TRADE (continued)
%% ========================================================================
\bilingualsection{卷九下 \quad 市易類（續）}{Fascicle 9, Part 2 \quad Trade (continued)}
\label{sec:fasc9b}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 4: Salt Pricing
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計求鹽價}{Salt Pricing}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問官鬻鹽，每袋重三百斤，成本一百貫。欲得利三成，問：每袋賣價幾何？
每斤賣價幾何？
\switchcolumn
The government sells salt. Each bag weighs 300 jin and costs 100 guan to
produce. A profit of 30\% is desired. Question: what is the selling price
per bag? What is the selling price per jin?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
每袋賣價若干貫，每斤若干文。
\switchcolumn
The selling price per bag is a certain number of guan; the price per jin is
a certain number of wen.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以成本乘利加成本，得賣價。術曰：以本為一，加三成為一三，以本乘之，得袋價。
以袋價除以斤數，得斤價。
\switchcolumn
Add the profit to the cost price to get the selling price. Method: take the
cost as unity, add three-tenths to get 1.3; multiply by the cost to get the
bag price. Divide the bag price by the number of jin to get the price per jin.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
成本$=100$貫，利$=30\%$

袋價：$100 \times 1.3 = 130$（貫）

斤價：$\dfrac{130000}{300} \approx 433.3$（文/斤）
\switchcolumn
Cost $= 100$ guan, profit $= 30\%$

Bag price: $100 \times 1.3 = 130$ (guan)

Price per jin: $\dfrac{130{,}000}{300} \approx 433.3$ (wen/jin)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 5: Equalizing Currency
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計均錢值}{Equalizing Currency}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問庫中舊錢三種：一曰足陌錢，陌法一千文；二曰九陌錢，陌法九百文；
三曰八陌錢，陌法八百文。今有足陌錢五百貫，九陌錢三百貫，八陌錢二百貫。
欲均為一陌，問：合一千文為陌，共得若干貫？
\switchcolumn
In the treasury there are three kinds of old currency: the first called
``full-bundle'' money (足陌錢), with 1000 wen per bundle; the second called
``nine-tenths'' money (九陌錢), with 900 wen per bundle; the third called
``eight-tenths'' money (八陌錢), with 800 wen per bundle. There are 500 guan
of full-bundle money, 300 guan of nine-tenths money, and 200 guan of
eight-tenths money. They are to be unified to a single standard. Question:
converting to the 1000-wen standard, how many guan are obtained in total?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
共得若干貫（足陌）。
\switchcolumn
The total obtained is a certain number of guan (full-bundle equivalent).
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以各陌錢數乘本陌法，得實際文數；并之；以足陌法一千除之，得共數。
\switchcolumn
Multiply each type of bundle money by its bundle rate to get the actual
number of wen; add them together; divide by the full-bundle standard of 1000
to get the total.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
足陌實數：$500 \times 1000 = 500{,}000$（文）

九陌實數：$300 \times 900 = 270{,}000$（文）

八陌實數：$200 \times 800 = 160{,}000$（文）

總實數：$500000 + 270000 + 160000 = 930{,}000$（文）

合足陌：$\dfrac{930000}{1000} = 930$（貫）
\switchcolumn
Full-bundle actual: $500 \times 1000 = 500{,}000$ (wen)

Nine-tenths actual: $300 \times 900 = 270{,}000$ (wen)

Eight-tenths actual: $200 \times 800 = 160{,}000$ (wen)

Total actual: $500{,}000 + 270{,}000 + 160{,}000 = 930{,}000$ (wen)

Converted to full-bundle: $\dfrac{930{,}000}{1000} = 930$ (guan)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 6: Setting Prices
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計定物價}{Setting Prices}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問有絲、綿、麻三物，共值八百貫。絲一斤價四貫，綿一斤價二貫，
麻一斤價五百文。欲買絲、綿、麻各若干斤，使價相等。問：各得幾何？
\switchcolumn
There are three commodities --- silk (絲), cotton floss (綿), and hemp (麻)
--- worth 800 guan in total. Silk costs 4 guan per jin, cotton floss 2 guan
per jin, and hemp 500 wen per jin. One wishes to buy certain quantities of
each so that the value of each commodity is equal. Question: how many jin of
each?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
絲若干斤，綿若干斤，麻若干斤。
\switchcolumn
A certain number of jin of silk, a certain number of jin of cotton floss,
and a certain number of jin of hemp.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以總價三而一，得每物之值。各以本價除之，得斤數。
\switchcolumn
Divide the total price by three to get the value of each commodity. Divide
by the respective price per jin to get the quantity in jin.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
每物之值：$\dfrac{800}{3} \approx 266.67$（貫）

絲斤數：$\dfrac{266.67}{4} \approx 66.67$（斤）

綿斤數：$\dfrac{266.67}{2} \approx 133.33$（斤）

麻斤數：$\dfrac{266.67}{0.5} = 533.33$（斤）
\switchcolumn
Value per commodity: $\dfrac{800}{3} \approx 266.67$ (guan)

Silk quantity: $\dfrac{266.67}{4} \approx 66.67$ (jin)

Cotton floss quantity: $\dfrac{266.67}{2} \approx 133.33$ (jin)

Hemp quantity: $\dfrac{266.67}{0.5} = 533.33$ (jin)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
%% PROBLEM 7: Profit on Transported Goods
%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\bilingualsubsection{計販運得利}{Profit on Transported Goods}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{問} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Question}}
\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
問一人持絹五百匹至遠方販賣。去時每匹價四貫，到彼時價漲五成。
回程買茶，茶價每斤三百文。問：賣絹得錢若干？可買茶若干斤？
\switchcolumn
A merchant carries 500 bolts of silk to a distant place for trade. The
purchase price was 4 guan per bolt; upon arrival, the price has risen by
50\%. On the return journey, he buys tea at 300 wen per jin. Question: how
much money does he obtain from selling the silk? How many jin of tea can he
buy?
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{答曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Answer}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
得錢若干貫，可買茶若干斤。
\switchcolumn
The money obtained is a certain number of guan; the tea that can be
purchased is a certain number of jin.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{術曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Method}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
以本價加利，得賣價；以匹數乘之，得總錢。以總錢除以茶價，得茶斤數。
\switchcolumn
Add the profit to the cost price to get the selling price; multiply by the
number of bolts to get the total money. Divide the total money by the tea
price to get the quantity of tea in jin.
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.4em}
\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{chinesecolor}{草曰} / \textcolor{englishcolor}{Working}}
\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{paracol}{2}
賣價：$4 \times 1.5 = 6$（貫/匹）

總錢：$500 \times 6 = 3000$（貫）$= 3{,}000{,}000$（文）

茶斤數：$\dfrac{3000000}{300} = 10000$（斤）
\switchcolumn
Selling price: $4 \times 1.5 = 6$ (guan/bolt)

Total money: $500 \times 6 = 3000$ (guan) $= 3{,}000{,}000$ (wen)

Tea quantity: $\dfrac{3{,}000{,}000}{300} = 10{,}000$ (jin)
\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}
\longline

\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Editorial Notes / 編者注}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection*{Units of Measurement / 度量衡表}

The problems in these fascicles employ traditional Chinese units:
本編算題所用度量衡，皆依宋制：

\vspace{0.5em}

\begin{center}
\begin{longtable}{llll}
\toprule
\textbf{Unit} & \textbf{Chinese} & \textbf{Pinyin} & \textbf{Approx.~Modern Value} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
Length & 丈 & zhang & $\approx 3.33$ metres \\
Length & 尺 & chi & $\approx 33.3$ centimetres \\
Length & 寸 & cun & $\approx 3.33$ centimetres \\
Area & 平方丈 & pingfang zhang & $\approx 11.09$ square metres \\
Volume & 立方丈 & lifang zhang & $\approx 37.0$ cubic metres \\
Volume & 立方尺 & lifang chi & $\approx 37.0$ litres \\
Capacity & 石 & dan/shi & $\approx 60$ kilograms (grain) \\
Capacity & 升 & sheng & $\approx 0.6$ litres \\
Weight & 斤 & jin & $\approx 600$ grams (Song) \\
Weight & 兩 & liang & $\approx 37.5$ grams \\
Weight & 錢 & qian & $\approx 3.75$ grams \\
Currency & 貫 & guan & 1000 wen (cash coins) \\
Currency & 文 & wen & Single cash coin \\
Distance & 里 & li & $\approx 556$ metres \\
Distance & 步 & bu & $\approx 1.54$ metres \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection*{Mathematical Methods / 數學方法}

\begin{paracol}{2}

數學九章所用算法，有數項獨創之術，尤以大衍求一術為最著。
本編營建、軍旅、市易三類，則多用體積公式、衰分術、重差術等。

\switchcolumn

The \textit{Shuxue Jiuzhang} employs several characteristic
mathematical techniques. The Construction, Military, and Trade fascicles
make extensive use of volume formulae, proportional distribution
(衰分), and the double-difference method (重差術).

\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}

\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Frustum volume formula (塹堵/臺積術):} For a rectangular frustum
  with upper dimensions $a \times b$, lower dimensions $c \times d$, and height $h$:
  \[
  V = \frac{h}{3}(ab + cd + ad + bc)
  \]
  This is equivalent to the modern prismatoid formula.

  \item \textbf{Proportional distribution (衰分/均輸術):} Problems involving
  allocation according to given ratios. Each party contributes in proportion
to their respective holding or capacity.

  \item \textbf{Double-difference method (重差術):} A trigonometric surveying
technique using two observations to determine distances and heights.

  \item \textbf{Currency conversion (陌法):} The ``bundle'' (陌) system of
currency conversion, reflecting the debased coinage of the Southern Song
period. One ``bundle'' (陌) nominally contained 1000 wen, but in practice
bundles of 900 or 800 wen were common.
\end{enumerate}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection*{Historical Context / 歷史背景}

\begin{paracol}{2}

秦九韶，字道古，生於南宋寧宗嘉泰二年（1202），卒於理宗景定二年（1261）。
所撰《數學九章》成書於淳祐七年（1247），時宋室南渡已百餘年，
國勢日蹙，蒙古鐵騎壓境。卷八軍旅之題，正反映當時岌岌可危之軍事情勢。

\switchcolumn

Qin Jiushao (ca.~1202--1261), styled Daogu, was one of the foremost
mathematicians of the Song Dynasty. The \textit{Shuxue Jiuzhang} was
completed in 1247, during the turbulent final decades of the Southern Song.
The military problems in Fascicle 8 directly reflect the desperate military
situation of the time, as the Song faced existential threats from the Mongols
under Genghis Khan and later Kublai Khan.

\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}

\begin{paracol}{2}

卷九市易之題，則反映南宋繁榮之商業經濟：紙幣交子會子之流通、
官營鹽茶之專賣、長途販運之興盛。此皆中古時期世界最發達之商業體系。

\switchcolumn

The trade problems in Fascicle 9 reflect the sophisticated commercial economy
of the Song, with its paper currency (交子, 會子), government monopolies on
salt and tea, and extensive long-distance trade networks. This was one of the
most advanced commercial systems in the medieval world.

\end{paracol}

\vspace{0.5em}

\begin{paracol}{2}

秦九韶自述其書：「大則可以通神明，順性命；小則可以經世務，類萬物。」
數學九章不獨為數學之鉅著，亦為研究宋代社會經濟軍事之重要史料。

\switchcolumn

Qin Jiushao described his own work: ``In the large sense it can communicate
with the divine and accord with the nature of things; in the small sense it
can govern worldly affairs and classify all things.'' The \textit{Shuxue
Jiuzhang} is not only a masterpiece of mathematics, but also an
important historical source for studying the society, economy, and military
of the Song Dynasty.

\end{paracol}

\vspace{2em}
\begin{center}
\longline
\vspace{1em}
{\small\color{sectioncolor}
\textit{--- End of Fascicles 7--9 / 卷七至卷九終 ---}
}
\end{center}

%% INTRODUCTION

\section{Introduction}

\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{\zh{關於本書}}\\[0.3em]
\zh{孫子算經}是中國現存最早的數學著作之一，成書於公元三世紀至五世紀之間。唐代將其列為\zh{算經十書}之一。作者孫子（「孫子」為尊稱）的身份至今仍不確定，但其生活年代遠早於《孫子兵法》的作者孫武。

全書共分三卷（\zh{卷}）：
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{\zh{卷上}}：度量衡單位、籌算記數法、乘除算法、九九乘法表
  \item \textbf{\zh{卷中}}：分數運算、幾何面積與體積計算
  \item \textbf{\zh{卷下}}：三十六道算題，包括著名的「物不知數」問題——\zh{中國剩餘定理}的最早記載
\end{itemize}

\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{About This Book}\\[0.3em]
The \textit{Sunzi Suanjing} (\zh{孫子算經}, ``Master Sun's Mathematical Manual'') is one of the earliest surviving Chinese mathematical texts, written during the 3rd to 5th centuries CE. It was listed as one of the \textit{Ten Computational Canons} (\zh{算經十書}) during the Tang dynasty. The identity of its author, Sunzi (``Master Sun''), remains unknown, though he lived much later than his namesake Sun Tzu, the author of \textit{The Art of War}.

The treatise consists of three volumes (\zh{卷}):
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Volume I} (\zh{卷上}): Units of measurement, counting rod notation, multiplication and division algorithms
  \item \textbf{Volume II} (\zh{卷中}): Fractions, geometry (areas, volumes), and practical problems
  \item \textbf{Volume III} (\zh{卷下}): 36 problems including the famous ``Problem of the Unknown Quantity''---the \textbf{Chinese Remainder Theorem}
\end{itemize}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\vspace{0.4cm}

\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{\zh{歷史意義}}\\[0.3em]
\zh{孫子算經}在數學史上佔有特殊的地位。其最著名的貢獻是\textbf{\zh{卷下}第26題}——「\zh{物不知數}」問題：

\begin{quote}
\zh{今有物，不知其數。三、三數之，賸二；五、五數之，賸三；七、七數之，賸二。問物幾何？}
\end{quote}

此問題提供了公式：
\[N = 70 r_1 + 21 r_2 + 15 r_3 - 105k\]
其中 $r_1, r_2, r_3$ 分別為以3、5、7除後的餘數。

\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Historical Significance}\\[0.3em]
The \textit{Sunzi Suanjing} holds a special place in the history of mathematics. Its most celebrated contribution is \textbf{Problem 26 of Volume III}:

\begin{quote}
\textit{``There are certain things whose number is unknown. If we count them by threes, we have two left over; by fives, we have three left over; and by sevens, two are left over. How many things are there?''}
\end{quote}

This problem provides the formula:
\[N = 70 r_1 + 21 r_2 + 15 r_3 - 105k\]
where $r_1, r_2, r_3$ are the remainders upon division by 3, 5, and 7.
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

%% PREFACE
%% ========================================================================
\section*{Preface 序}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Preface (序)}

\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{\zh{孫子序}}\\[0.5em]
\zh{孫子曰：夫算者，天地之經緯，群生之元首；五常之本末，陰陽之父母；星辰之建號，三光之表裹；五行之準平，四時之終始；萬物之祖宗，六藝之綱紀。}

\zh{稽群倫之聚散，考二氣之降升；推寒暑之迭運，步遠近之殊同；觀天道精微之兆基，察地理從橫之長短；采神祇之所在，極成敗之符驗；窮道德之理，究性命之情。}

\zh{立規矩，準方圓，謹法度，約尺丈，立權衡，平重輕，剖毫釐，析黍絫；歷億載而不朽，施八極而無疆。散之不可勝究，斂之不盈掌握。}

\zh{嚮之者富有餘，背之者貧且窶；心開者幼沖而即悟，意閉者皓首而難精。夫欲學之者必務量能揆己，志在所專。如是則焉有不成者哉。}

\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Preface by Sunzi}\\[0.5em]
Sun Zi said: Calculation is the meridian and latitude of heaven and earth, the origin and head of all living beings; the root and branch of the Five Constants, the father and mother of yin and yang; the establishment of titles for stars and constellations, the exterior and interior of the Three Lights; the standard balance of the Five Elements, the beginning and end of the Four Seasons; the ancestors of all things, the framework and discipline of the Six Arts.

Investigate the gathering and dispersing of all categories, examine the descending and ascending movements of the Two Qi; track the alternating cycles of cold and heat, pace the differences and similarities between near and far; observe the subtle omens and foundations of the heavenly Dao, examine the lengths and widths of the horizontal and vertical features of geography; gather signs of where gods and spirits reside, thoroughly test omens of success and failure; exhaust the principles of virtue and morality, investigate the nature and essence of life.

Establish rules and compasses, standardize squares and circles, observe laws and regulations carefully, measure with precision in \textit{chi} and \textit{zhang}, set up weights and balances, equalize the heavy and light, dissect thousandths of an inch, analyze grains accumulated one by one; enduring through countless generations without decay, its influence extends to all directions without limit. When dispersed, it is beyond full comprehension; when gathered, it does not fill the palm of one's hand.

Those who face toward it are rich with abundance, while those who turn away from it are poor and destitute; those whose minds open understand even as children, while those whose intentions remain closed find mastery difficult even with a white beard. Therefore, one who wishes to study must necessarily measure his own ability and assess himself carefully, setting his mind on specialization in a particular field. If so, how could there be any failure?
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}

\section{Volume I 卷上}

\subsection*{1.\ Length Measurements 度之所起}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{度之所起，起於忽。欲知其忽，蠶所生，吐絲為忽。十忽為一秒，十秒為一毫，十毫為一釐，十釐為一分，十分為一寸，十寸為一尺，十尺為一丈，十丈為一引；五十尺為一端；四十尺為一疋；六尺為一步。二百四十步為一畝。三百步為一里。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{The origin of measurement begins with the ``hu'' (\zh{忽}). To understand the hu, it is said that silkworms produce it by spinning silk. Ten hu make one miao (\zh{秒}), ten miao make one hao (\zh{毫}), ten hao make one li (\zh{釐}), ten li make one fen (\zh{分}), ten fen make one cun (\zh{寸}), ten cun make one chi (\zh{尺}), ten chi make one zhang (\zh{丈}), and ten zhang make one yin (\zh{引}); fifty chi make one duan (\zh{端}); forty chi make one pi (\zh{疋}); six chi make one bu (\zh{步}). Two hundred and forty bu make one mu (\zh{畝}). Three hundred bu make one li (\zh{里}).}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{2.\ Weight and Capacity 稱量之所起}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{稱之所起，起於黍。十黍為一絫，十絫為一銖，二十四銖為一兩，十六兩為一斤，三十斤為一鉤，四鉤為一石。量之所起，起於粟。六粟為一圭，十圭為一抄，十抄為一撮，十撮為一勺，十勺為一合，十合為一升，十升為一斗，十斗為一斛。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{The origin of weight begins with the grain of millet (\zh{黍}). Ten millet grains make one lei (\zh{絫}), ten lei make one zhu (\zh{銖}), twenty-four zhu make one liang (\zh{兩}), sixteen liang make one jin (\zh{斤}), thirty jin make one jun (\zh{鉤}), and four jun make one dan (\zh{石}). The origin of capacity begins with the grain of millet. Six millet grains make one gui (\zh{圭}), ten gui make one chao (\zh{抄}), ten chao make one cuo (\zh{撮}), ten cuo make one shao (\zh{勺}), ten shao make one ge (\zh{合}), ten ge make one sheng (\zh{升}), ten sheng make one dou (\zh{斗}), and ten dou make one hu (\zh{斛}).}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{3.\ Large Numbers 大數之法}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{凡大數之法，萬萬曰億，萬萬億曰兆，萬萬兆曰京，萬萬京曰陔，萬萬陔曰秭，萬萬秭曰壤，萬萬壤曰溝，萬萬溝曰澗，萬萬澗日正，萬萬正曰載。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Generally, the method for large numbers: ten thousand times ten thousand is yi (\zh{億}, $10^8$); ten thousand times yi is zhao (\zh{兆}, $10^{16}$); ten thousand times zhao is jing (\zh{京}, $10^{24}$); and so on up to zai (\zh{載}, $10^{80}$).}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{4.\ Geometric Ratios 方圓之比}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{周三徑一。方五邪七；見邪求方，五之，七而一；見方求邪，七之，五而一。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{The circumference of a circle is three times its diameter ($\pi \approx 3$). A square with side length five has a diagonal of seven; to find the side from the diagonal, multiply by five and divide by seven; to find the diagonal from the side, multiply by seven and divide by five.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{5.\ Weights of Materials 物之輕重}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{黃金方寸重一斤。白金方寸重一十四兩。玉方寸重一十二兩。銅方寸重七兩半。鈆方寸重九兩半。鐵方寸重六兩。石方寸重三兩。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{One cubic cun of gold weighs one jin. One cubic cun of silver weighs fourteen liang. One cubic cun of jade weighs twelve liang. One cubic cun of copper weighs seven and a half liang. One cubic cun of lead weighs nine and a half liang. One cubic cun of iron weighs six liang. One cubic cun of stone weighs three liang.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{6.\ Counting Rod Notation 筭位之制}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{凡筭之法，先識其位，一從十橫，百立千僵，千十相望，萬百相當。}

\vspace{0.2cm}
\textbf{\zh{籌算記數法：}}\zh{個位（1--9）縱式；十位（10--90）橫式；百位（100--900）縱式；千位（1000--9000）橫式。縱橫交替，以定位值。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{The method for calculation begins by identifying the positions: one is vertical, ten is horizontal; a hundred stands upright and a thousand lies flat.}

\vspace{0.2cm}
\textbf{Counting Rod Numeral System:} Units (1--9): \textbf{vertical}; Tens (10--90): \textbf{horizontal}; Hundreds (100--900): \textbf{vertical}; Thousands (1000--9000): \textbf{horizontal}. The pattern alternates.
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{7.\ Method of Multiplication 乘法}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{凡乘之法，重置其位。上下相觀，上位有十步至十，有百步至百，有千步至千。以上命下，所得之數列於中位。言十即過，不滿自如。上位乘訖者先去之。下位乘訖者則俱退之。六不積，五不隻。上下相乘，至盡則已。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{In multiplication, the positions are arranged again for calculation. By observing vertically and horizontally, if the upper position has ten, it moves to the tens place; if it has a hundred, it moves to the hundreds place; if it has a thousand, it moves to the thousands place. The upper number is used to multiply the lower one, and the resulting product is placed in the middle position. If it reaches ten, carry over; if less than ten, leave as is. After the upper position has been multiplied, remove it first. Once the lower position is multiplied, both are moved back. Six does not accumulate; five does not count as a single unit. Multiplying vertically and horizontally continues until the end is reached.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{8.\ Method of Division 除法}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{凡除之法，與乘正異。乘得在中央，除得在上方。假令六為法，百為實。以六除百，當進之二等，令在正百下，以六除一，則法多而實少，不可除，故當退就十位。以法除實，言一六而折百為四十，故可除。若實多法少，自當百之，不當復退。故或步法十者置於十位，百者置於百位。上位有空絕者，法退二位。餘法皆如乘時。實有餘者，以法命之，以法為母。實餘為子。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{The method of division differs from multiplication. In multiplication, the result is placed in the center; in division, it appears at the top. Suppose six is the divisor (法) and one hundred is the dividend (實). Dividing one hundred by six, it should be advanced two positions and placed under the hundreds place. Dividing one by six results in a larger divisor than dividend, which is not possible; therefore, we must retreat to the tens position. Using the divisor to divide the dividend: saying ``one six'' and reducing a hundred by sixty results in forty, so division is possible. If the dividend is large and the divisor small, it naturally belongs to the hundreds place, and there is no need to retreat further. Therefore, if a step of ten is taken, it should be placed in the tens position; if a hundred, in the hundreds position. If there is an empty space at the upper position, the divisor must retreat two positions. The remaining methods follow those of multiplication. If there is a remainder in the dividend, name it using the divisor as the denominator. The remainder becomes the numerator.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

\subsection*{9.\ Example: $81 \times 81$ 九九八十一自乘}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{九九八十一，自相乘，得幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：六千五百六十一。}
\shu\zh{術曰：重置其位，以上八呼下八，八八六十四，即下六千四百於中位。以上八呼下一，一八如八，即於中位下八十。退下位一等，收上位八十。以上位一呼下八，一八如八，即於中位下八十。以上一呼下一，一一如一，即於中位下一。上下位俱收，中位即得六千五百六十一。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Ninety-nine times eighty-one, when multiplied by itself, results in what?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Six thousand five hundred and sixty-one.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Arrange the positions again, call out eight from above to multiply with eight below; eight eights are sixty-four. Place six thousand four hundred in the middle position. Call out eight from above to one below, one eight is eight; place eighty in the middle position. Move the lower position back by one rank and collect the upper value of eighty. Call out one from above to eight below, one eight is eight, place eighty in the middle position accordingly. Call out one from the upper position to multiply with one from the lower; one times one is one, so place one in the middle position. After collecting both the upper and lower positions, the middle position yields six thousand five hundred sixty-one.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $81 \times 81 = (80 + 1)^2 = 6400 + 80 + 80 + 1 = 6561$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{10.\ Example: $6561 \div 9$ 九人分之}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{六千五百六十一，九人分之，問人得幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：七百二十九。}
\shu\zh{術曰：先置六千五百六十一於中位，為實。下列九人為法。上位置七百，以上七呼下九，七九六十三，即除中位六千三百。退下位一等，即上位置二十。以上二呼下九，二九十八，即除中位一百八十。又更退下位一等，即上位更置九，即以上九呼下九，九九八十一，即除中位八十一。中位盡，收下位。上位所得即人之所得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Six thousand five hundred sixty-one is to be divided among nine people; how much does each person receive?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Seven hundred and twenty-nine.}
\shuE\textit{Method: First place six thousand five hundred sixty-one in the middle position as the dividend (實). Place nine people below as the divisor (法). Place seven hundred in the upper position; call out seven from above to multiply by nine below, seven nines are sixty-three, and subtract six thousand three hundred from the middle. Move the lower position back one rank; place twenty in the upper position. Call out two from above to multiply by nine from below, two nines are eighteen, and subtract one hundred eighty from the middle. Move the lower position back another rank, place nine in the upper position again. Call out nine from above to multiply by nine below; nine nines are eighty-one and subtract eighty-one from the middle. When the middle position is exhausted, collect the lower positions. The result in the upper position is what each person receives.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $6561 \div 9 = 729$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

\section{Volume II 卷中}

\subsection*{1.\ Reducing Fractions 約分}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有一十八分之一十二。問約之得幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：三分之二。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置十八分在下，一十二分在上。副置二位，以少減多，等數得六，為法。約之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is twelve eighteenths. Ask: reducing it, what does it equal?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Two thirds.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place eighteen parts below and twelve parts above. Set up both positions, subtract the smaller from the larger; the equal number (等數, GCD) obtained is six, which is the divisor. Reduce by it, and you obtain the answer.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $\frac{12}{18} = \frac{12 \div 6}{18 \div 6} = \frac{2}{3}$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{2.\ Grain Conversion 粟米換算}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有粟一斗，問為糲米幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：六升。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置粟一斗，十升。以糲米率三十乘之，得三百升，為實。以粟率五十為法，除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is one dou of millet. How much coarse rice does it make?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Six sheng.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place one dou of millet, which equals ten sheng. Multiply by the coarse rice rate of thirty to get three hundred sheng, as the dividend. Use the millet rate of fifty as the divisor and divide; thus you obtain the answer.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $10 \times 30 \div 50 = 6$ sheng.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{3.\ Brick Calculation 積磚之數}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有屋基南北三丈，東西六丈，欲以磚砌之。凡積二尺，用磚五枚。問計幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：四千五百枚。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置東西六丈，以南北三丈乘之，得一千八百尺。以五乘之，得九千尺。以二除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a house foundation with a north-south length of three zhang and an east-west width of six zhang, and one wishes to build it using bricks. Generally for every two cubic chi in volume, five bricks are used. Ask how many will be needed?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Four thousand five hundred bricks.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the east-west length of six zhang, multiply it by the north-south length of three zhang to get one thousand eight hundred chi. Multiply it by five to get nine thousand chi. Divide it by two, and you will obtain the answer.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Area $= 30 \times 60 = 1800$ sq~chi. Bricks $= 1800 \times 5 / 2 = 4500$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{4.\ Area of a Circular Field 圓田面積}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有圓田周三百步，徑一百步。問得田幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：三十一畝奇六十步。}
\shu\zh{術曰：先置周三百步，半之，得一百五十步。又置徑一百步，半之，得五十步。相乘，得七千五百步。以畝法二百四十步除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a round field with circumference three hundred bu, diameter one hundred bu. Ask how much land does it amount to?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Thirty-one mu and sixty bu extra.}
\shuE\textit{Method: First place the circumference of three hundred bu, halve it to get one hundred fifty bu. Also place the diameter of one hundred bu, halve it, getting fifty bu. Multiply them together to get seven thousand five hundred bu. Divide it by the mu standard of two hundred forty bu, and you will obtain the area.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Area $\approx \frac{C}{2} \times \frac{d}{2} = 150 \times 50 = 7500$ sq~bu $= 31$ mu + 60 bu.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{5.\ Square Field with Mulberry 方田桑生中央}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有方田，桑生中央。從角至桑一百四十七步。問為田幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：一頃八十三畝奇一百八十步。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置角至桑一百四十七步，倍之，得二百九十四步。以五乘之，得一千四百七十步。以七除之，得二百一十步。自相乘，得四萬四千一百步。以二百四十步除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a square field with mulberry trees growing in the center. From the corner to the mulberry tree is one hundred forty-seven steps. Ask how much field does it amount to?}
\daE\textit{Answer: One qing, eighty-three mu and one hundred eighty steps extra.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the distance from corner to mulberry tree as one hundred forty-seven bu, double it to get two hundred ninety-four bu. Multiply it by five to get one thousand four hundred seventy steps. Divide it by seven, getting two hundred ten steps. Multiply it by itself to get forty-four thousand one hundred bu. Divide it by two hundred forty steps, and you will get the result.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Diagonal = 147 bu. Using $\sqrt{2} \approx \frac{7}{5}$, side $s = 147 \times 2 \times \frac{5}{7} = 210$ bu. Area $= 210^2 = 44100$ sq~bu.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

\section{Volume III 卷下}

\subsection*{1.\ Rent Distribution 九家共輸租}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有甲、乙、丙、丁、戊、己、庚、辛、壬九家共輸租。甲出三十五斛，乙出四十六斛，丙出五十七斛，丁出六十八斛，戊出七十九斛，己出八十斛，庚出一百斛，辛出二百一十斛，壬出三百二十五斛。凡九家共輸租一千斛。僦運直折二百斛外，問家各幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：甲二十八斛。乙三十六斛八蚪。丙四十五斛六蚪。丁五十四斛四蚪。戊六十三斛二蚪。己六十四斛。庚八十斛。辛一百六十八斛。壬二百六十斛。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置甲出三十五斛，以四乘之，得一百四十斛。以五除之，得二十八斛。……}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are nine families jointly paying rent: Jia 35 hu, Yi 46 hu, Bing 57 hu, Ding 68 hu, Wu 79 hu, Ji 80 hu, Geng 100 hu, Xin 210 hu, Ren 325 hu. Total 1,000 hu. After deducting transport cost of 200 hu, how much should each family contribute?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Jia 28 hu, Yi 36 hu 8 dou, Bing 45 hu 6 dou, Ding 54 hu 4 dou, Wu 63 hu 2 dou, Ji 64 hu, Geng 80 hu, Xin 168 hu, Ren 260 hu.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Take each family's contribution, multiply by four, and divide by five.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} After 200 hu deduction, 800 hu remains. Each pays $4/5$ of original.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{2.\ Pile of Millet 平地聚粟}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有平地聚粟，下周三丈六尺，高四尺五寸。問粟幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：一百斛。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置周三丈六尺，自相乘，得一千二百九十六尺。以高四尺五寸乘之，得五千八百三十二尺。以三十六除之，得一百六十二尺。以斛法一尺六寸二分除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a pile of millet on level ground, with base circumference of three zhang six chi and height of four chi five cun. How much millet is there?}
\daE\textit{Answer: One hundred hu.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the circumference of three zhang six chi, multiply it by itself to get 1296 chi. Multiply by the height of 4 chi 5 cun to get 5832 chi. Divide by 36 to get 162 chi. Divide by the hu standard of 1 chi 6 cun 2 fen.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Volume $\approx \frac{C^2 \times h}{36} = \frac{1296 \times 4.5}{36} = 162$ cu~chi. $162 \div 1.62 = 100$ hu.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{3.\ Go Board 碁局}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有碁局方一十九道。問用碁幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：三百六十一。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置一十九道，自相乘之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a Go board with a square pattern of nineteen lines on each side. How many pieces (intersections) are there?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Three hundred sixty-one.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Take the nineteen lines, multiply them by themselves, and you get the result.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $19^2 = 361$ intersection points on a Go board.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{4.\ People and Carts 人與車}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有三人共車，二車空；二人共車，九人步。問人與車各幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：一十五車。三十九人。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置二車，以三乘之，得六。加步者九人，得車一十五。欲知人者，以二乘車，加九人，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are three people sharing a cart, and two carts remain empty; two people share another cart, while nine people walk. What are the numbers of people and carts?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Fifteen carts, thirty-nine people.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place two carts, multiply by three to get six. Add the nine people who walk, getting fifteen carts. To find the number of people, multiply two by the number of carts and add nine people.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $3(c-2) = p$ and $2c + 9 = p$, giving $c = 15$, $p = 39$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{5.\ Guests at a Feast 婦人河上蕩桮}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有婦人河上蕩桮。津吏問曰：「桮何以多？」婦人曰：「家有客。」津吏曰：「客幾何？」婦人曰：「二人共飯，三人共羹，四人共肉，凡用桮六十五。不知客幾何？」}
\da\zh{答曰：六十人。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置六十五桮，以一十二乘之，得七百八十，以十三除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a woman washing cups at the riverbank. The ferry official asked, ``Why so many cups?'' The woman replied, ``There are guests at my home.'' ``How many guests?'' ``Two people share a meal, three share soup, four share meat, and in total sixty-five cups are used.''}
\daE\textit{Answer: Sixty people.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Take the 65 cups, multiply by twelve to get 780, then divide by thirteen.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Each uses $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{13}{12}$ cups. $65 \div \frac{13}{12} = 60$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

\subsection*{6.\ Wood and Rope 木與繩}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有木，不知長短。引繩度之，餘繩四尺五寸。屈繩量之，不足一尺。問木長幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：六尺五寸。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置餘繩四尺五寸，加不足一尺，共五尺五寸。倍之，得一丈一尺。減餘四尺五寸，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is a piece of wood whose length is unknown. Using a rope to measure it, the rope has 4 chi 5 cun left over. Folding the rope to measure it results in one chi short. What is the length of the wood?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Six chi and five cun.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the excess rope of 4 chi 5 cun, add the deficit of 1 chi, obtaining 5 chi 5 cun. Double it to get 1 zhang 1 chi. Subtract the excess of 4 chi 5 cun.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $R = W + 4.5$ and $R/2 = W - 1$. Solving: $W = 6.5$ chi.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{7.\ Rice in a Vessel 器中米}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有器中米，不知其數。前人取半，中人三分取一，後人四分取一，餘米一斗五升。問本米幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：六斗。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置餘米一斗五升，以六乘之，得九斗。以二除之，得四斗五升。以四乘之，得一斛八斗。以三除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is rice in a vessel, but its quantity is unknown. The first person took half, the second took one-third of what remained, the third took one-fourth of what was left, and there were 1 dou 5 sheng remaining. What was the original amount?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Six dou.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the remaining rice of 1 dou 5 sheng, multiply by six to get 9 dou. Divide by two to get 4 dou 5 sheng. Multiply by four to get 1 hu 8 dou. Divide by three.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{4} \times x = \frac{x}{4} = 1.5$ dou. So $x = 6$ dou.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{8.\ Birds and Beasts 獸六首四足}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有獸六首四足，禽四首二足。上有七十六首，下有四十六足。問禽、獸各幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：八獸，七禽。}
\shu\zh{術曰：倍足以減首，餘，半之，即禽。四乘禽數，減足，餘，半之，即獸。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are beasts with six heads and four feet, and birds with four heads and two feet. Above there are seventy-six heads, below there are forty-six feet. Ask: How many birds and beasts are there?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Eight beasts, seven birds.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Double the feet and subtract the heads; halve the remainder to get the number of birds. Multiply the number of birds by four, subtract from the feet; halve the remainder to get the number of beasts.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $6b + 4i = 76$, $4b + 2i = 46$. Solving: $b = 8$, $i = 7$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{9.\ One Hundred Deer 百鹿入城}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有百鹿入城，家取一鹿，不盡；又三家共一鹿，適盡。問城中家幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：七十五家。}
\shu\zh{術曰：以盈不足取之。假令七十二家，鹿不盡四。令之九十家，鹿不足二十。置七十二於右上，盈四於右下。置九十於左上，不足二十於左下。維乘之，所得，并為實。并盈不足為法。除之，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are one hundred deer entering a city; each household takes one deer, but they do not finish; then three households share one deer and it is just finished. Ask: How many households are in the city?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Seventy-five households.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Use the surplus-and-deficit method. Suppose 72 households: 4 deer remain (surplus). Suppose 90: 20 deer short (deficit). Cross-multiply and add to get the dividend. Add surplus and deficit to get the divisor.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $h + h/3 = 100$, so $4h/3 = 100$, giving $h = 75$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\newpage

\subsection*{10.\ Pheasants and Rabbits 雉兔同籠}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有雉、兔同籠，上有三十五頭，下九十四足。問雉、兔各幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：雉二十三。兔一十二。}
\shu\zh{術曰：上置三十五頭，下置九十四足。半其足，得四十七。以少減多，再命之，上三除下三，上五除下五。下有一除上一，下有二除上二，即得。}

\zh{又術曰：上置頭，下置足。半其足，以頭除足，以足除頭，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are pheasants and rabbits in a cage, with thirty-five heads above and ninety-four feet below. Ask: How many pheasants and how many rabbits are there?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Twenty-three pheasants, twelve rabbits.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place thirty-five heads above, ninety-four feet below. Halve the feet to get forty-seven. Subtract the smaller from the larger, and command it again.}

\textit{Alternative method: Place heads above, feet below. Halve the feet, use heads to remove feet and feet to remove heads.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} $p + r = 35$, $2p + 4r = 94$. Solving: $p = 23$, $r = 12$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{11.\ Nine Dikes 出門望見九隄}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有出門望見九隄。隄有九木，木有九枝，枝有九巢，巢有九禽，禽有九雛，雛有九毛，毛有九色。問各幾何？}
\da\zh{答曰：木八十一。枝七百二十九。巢六千五百六十一。禽五萬九千四十九。雛五十三萬一千四百四十一。毛四百七十八萬二千九百六十九。色四千三百四萬六千七百二十一。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置九隄，以九乘之，得木之數。又以九乘之，得枝之數。又以九乘之，得巢之數。又以九乘之，得禽之數。又以九乘之，得雛之數。又以九乘之，得毛之數。又以九乘之，得色之數。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there is someone who goes out of the gate and sees nine dikes. Each dike has nine trees, each tree has nine branches, each branch has nine nests, each nest has nine birds, each bird has nine chicks, each chick has nine feathers, and each feather has nine colors. Ask: How many of each are there?}
\daE\textit{Answer: 81 trees, 729 branches, 6,561 nests, 59,049 birds, 531,441 chicks, 4,782,969 feathers, 43,046,721 colors.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place nine dikes, multiply by nine to get the number of trees. Multiply by nine again for each successive level.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} Powers of nine: $9^2 = 81$, $9^3 = 729$, $9^4 = 6561$, $9^5 = 59049$, $9^6 = 531441$, $9^7 = 4782969$, $9^8 = 43046721$.}
\end{minipage}}
\vspace{0.5em}


\subsection*{12.\ Three Daughters 三女歸家}
\noindent\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wen\zh{今有三女，長女五日一歸，中女四日一歸，少女三日一歸。問三女幾何日相會？}
\da\zh{答曰：六十日。}
\shu\zh{術曰：置長女五日、中女四日、少女三日，於右方。各列一算於左方。維乘之，各得所到數：長女十二到，中女十五到，少女二十到。又各以歸日乘到數，即得。}
\end{minipage}}%
\hfill
\fcolorbox{rulecolor}{white}{%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\wenE\textit{Now there are three daughters: the eldest returns home every five days, the middle every four days, and the youngest every three days. Ask: After how many days will the three daughters meet again?}
\daE\textit{Answer: Sixty days.}
\shuE\textit{Method: Place the eldest daughter's five days, the middle daughter's four days, and the youngest daughter's three days on the right side. Place one counter for each on the left side. Multiply them, and you get their respective numbers of arrivals: twelve, fifteen, and twenty. Then multiply each return day by the number of arrivals.}

\textit{\textbf{Modern:} This is the least common multiple: $\text{lcm}(3,4,5) = 60$.}
\end{minipage}}
